entries.summary: The members that make it a seekable, readable and writable `Stream` over one pooled buffer. They copy straight to and from the pooled buffer through no shared array, and the async members complete synchronously. Writing past the end zero-fills the gap, and `SetLength` zeroes the bytes it cuts off. After `Dispose`, `CanRead`, `CanSeek` and `CanWrite` are `false`.
entries.throws: `ObjectDisposedException` when the stream has been disposed, from every member here except `CanRead`, `CanSeek`, `CanWrite`, `Flush` and `FlushAsync`; `ReadAsync` and `WriteAsync` return a canceled task instead when their token is canceled. `IOException` when a seek would move the position before the start of the stream, or a write would end past `Array.MaxLength`. `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when a position or length is negative or more than `Array.MaxLength`.

entries.summary: A growable builder for text that keeps its characters in a pooled buffer, and zeroes them when it releases the buffer if it is sensitive. It is a `ref struct`, so it stays on the stack and cannot cross an `await`. Pass it by `ref` and never copy it.

Starts the builder with a buffer rented from the pool that `isSensitive` selects, rented up front when `initialCapacity` is more than 0 and otherwise on the first append, or with a span you provide, such as a `stackalloc` span, that the builder zeroes when it leaves it if it is sensitive. The parameterless constructor makes an empty builder that is not sensitive.
entries.throws: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `initialCapacity` is negative.

entries.summary: Whether the builder zeroes its buffers when it releases them, and rents them from the secure pool.
The number of characters written so far. It is 0 after `Reset` and `Dispose`.
The number of characters the current buffer can hold. It is 0 when the builder has no buffer.

The characters written so far as a `ReadOnlySpan<char>`. It is not valid after an append that grows the buffer, after `Reset`, or after `Dispose`, but it is valid as the argument of an append to the same builder. Use it for sensitive text, so that the text never becomes a `string`.

entries.throws: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `length` is negative.

entries.summary: Zeroes the written part of the buffer, sets the length to zero and keeps the buffer.

Releases the buffer, zeroing it when the builder is sensitive, and leaves the builder empty. When the buffer is a span passed to the constructor, a sensitive builder zeroes all of it. The builder can be used again, and then it rents a new buffer.

entries.summary: Makes a `string` from the characters written so far. A `string` cannot be zeroed, so the copy stays in memory until the garbage collector reclaims it, even when the builder is sensitive. Call it only when the text is not sensitive, and use `WrittenSpan` otherwise.

entries.summary: Creates a `Secret<T>` in a sensitive buffer, either as a copy of `value` or of `length` elements that `action` fills in place, so the value never needs a second copy. The caller must dispose the secret, and still owns `value`. When `action` throws, the buffer is zeroed and returned, and the exception is rethrown.
entries.throws: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `length` is negative. `ArgumentNullException` when `action` is null.

entries.summary: Holds a secret value in a sensitive buffer, hides it from `ToString` and the debugger, compares it in fixed time, and zeroes it when disposed. It lives in memory only: it is not serializable and it is not key storage. It is not thread-safe against `Dispose`.
The number of elements in the secret. Reading it does not reveal the contents, and it works after `Dispose`.
Returns the secret as a `ReadOnlySpan<T>`. This is the one way to read the secret. The span is valid until the secret is disposed.
entries.throws: `ObjectDisposedException` when the secret has been disposed.

entries.summary: Returns the secret as a `ReadOnlyMemory<T>`, for callers that cannot hold a span. The memory is valid until the secret is disposed.
entries.throws: `ObjectDisposedException` when the secret has been disposed.

entries.summary: Copies the secret to `destination`. The copy is not a secret that the library tracks, so zero it when the secret is sensitive.
entries.throws: `ArgumentException` when `destination` is shorter than `Length`. `ObjectDisposedException` when the secret has been disposed.

entries.summary: Compares the secret to a span in time that does not depend on where they first differ. It returns `true` only when the lengths and the contents match. Spans of different lengths return `false` at once, so it does not hide the length.
entries.throws: `ObjectDisposedException` when the secret has been disposed.

entries.summary: Compares the contents of two secrets in fixed time. It returns `true` when the other secret is the same instance, or has the same length and contents, and `false` for null. `GetHashCode` returns `Length`, so the hash code reveals nothing about the contents.
entries.throws: `ObjectDisposedException` when this secret or the other one has been disposed, also when the other one is this secret; comparing with null returns `false`.

entries.summary: Returns `[REDACTED]`, never the secret, so a secret that is logged or inspected does not leak.
Zeroes the secret and returns its buffer. Calling it again does nothing. Afterwards `Reveal`, `RevealMemory`, `CopyTo`, `FixedTimeEquals` and `Equals` throw `ObjectDisposedException`.

Names the `Meter` through which NCode.Buffers reports its metrics: the counters `ncode.buffers.secure_pool.rentals`, `ncode.buffers.secure_pool.returns` and `ncode.buffers.secure_pool.trimmed`. Recording costs nothing until a listener subscribes.
The name of the meter, `NCode.Buffers`. One meter serves the whole process. A host subscribes to it with OpenTelemetry's `AddMeter(BufferMetrics.MeterName)`.
